subject.title: Visible inbound channel turn can be silently dropped: zero-payload dispatch has no retry, dead-letter, or user-visible failure

question: For a visible inbound turn that returns zero payloads, should OpenClaw treat an uncompleted dedupe/aborted claimant as a recoverable failed inbound event, or retain current suppression semantics and add diagnostics only?
rationale: The safe recovery boundary depends on whether duplicate suppression and aborts may still produce a later successful reply; source inspection cannot choose that user-visible retry and acknowledgement policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Define durable ownership, then recover
options.body: Record claimant completion atomically and enqueue or dead-letter only a visible turn whose winning claimant never completed.

options.title: Observability-only first
options.body: Propagate a terminal reason into logs and telemetry, preserving current behavior until incidents identify a recovery-safe subset.

options.title: Always send a failure acknowledgement
options.body: Emit a minimal resend notice for every visible zero-count dispatch, accepting possible false alarms for benign duplicate or abort paths.

recommendation.title: Define durable ownership, then recover
recommendation.body: Record claimant completion atomically and enqueue or dead-letter only a visible turn whose winning claimant never completed.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent iMessage catchup and source-conversation work makes this the closest available routing candidate, although generic dispatch ownership remains uncertain.
